tenuicruris:study:1.title: Tenuicruris piscanexum , a new addition to Australia’s rare Cretaceous bird fossils (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Tenuicruris lived during the Early Cretaceous Albian age.
The fossils of Tenuicruris come from the Toolebuc Formation in Australia.
Tenuicruris is an extinct enantiornithean bird known from a single isolated leg bone.
facts.quote: known from a single isolated leg bone

facts.statement: The specimen is a nearly complete left tibiotarsus and is housed in the Kronosaurus Korner Museum as KK F1451.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Kronosaurus Korner Museum, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen KK F1451. It consists of a nearly complete left tibiotarsus.

facts.statement: The generic name Tenuicruris combines Latin tenuis (slender) and cruris (leg), and the species name piscanexum combines piscis (fish) and nexum (binding).
facts.quote: The generic name, Tenuicruris, combines the Latin words tenuis, meaning slender, and cruris, meaning leg. The specific name, piscanexum, is a combination of the Latin piscis, meaning fish, and nexum, meaning binding

facts.statement: The holotype tibiotarsus measures 6.54 cm in length.
facts.quote: The T. piscanexum holotype tibiotarsus is 6.54 cm long.

facts.statement: Nanantius, a contemporaneous Australian enantiornithean, has a tibiotarsus about half that size (3.14 cm).
facts.quote: In the coeval Nanantius, this bone is about half the size, at 3.14 cm.

facts.statement: Tenuicruris is distinguished by a deep fossa on the lateral surface of the tibiotarsus near the distal condyle.
facts.quote: a deep fossa (depression) on the lateral (outer) surface of the tibiotarsus proximal to the distal condyle

facts.statement: Tenuicruris also has distal condyles that are flared when viewed from behind.
facts.quote: distal condyles that are flared when seen from behind

facts.statement: Tenuicruris shares a prominent craniolateral cnemial crest with the Chinese taxa Monoenantiornis and Qiliania.
facts.quote: presence of a prominent craniolateral cnemial crest, between Tenuicruris and Monoenantiornis and Qiliania

facts.statement: Tenuicruris is the second Mesozoic bird to be named from Australia.
facts.quote: It is the second Mesozoic bird named from Australia.

facts.statement: It is thought that Tenuicruris inhabited the Eromanga Sea, an extensive inland sea of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: se cree que habitó el Mar de Eromanga

rejected.statement: Tenuicruris was named as a new genus and species by White et al. in 2026.
The holotype specimen (KK F1451) was discovered about 12 km northwest of Richmond, Queensland, in the public Dig Site 1.
rejected.quote: The Tenuicruris fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Toolebuc Formation about 12 km northwest of Richmond in Queensland, Australia. This site, called 'Dig Site 1', is a public fossicking area.

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic analysis placed Tenuicruris as an indeterminate, non‑pengornithid enantiornithean due to limited data, resulting in an unresolved polytomy.
rejected.quote: White et al. regarded Tenuricruris as an indeterminate, non-pengornithid enantiornithean. ... resulted in a large, unresolved polytomy of most included enantiornitheans.
